collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Visiting researchers want to watch the village's private naming rite: explain it is private, or invite them to part of it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Researchers from another island have asked to watch the village's naming rite, which is only ever seen by the family. They promise to be quiet. (friend), a researcher (friend.him/her)self, understands their curiosity. (subject) says curiosity is not permission. What should the village say?

choices.label: Invite Them to Part of It

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) explains to the researchers that some things are kept, not hidden. The researchers are disappointed, but they listen, and write down only that the rite exists and belongs to the families. (friend) thinks that is exactly right.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The family agrees to let the researchers see the feast afterwards, not the rite itself. The researchers eat a great deal and ask a great many questions, most of which are politely not answered. Everyone goes home satisfied.
